findings.businessImpact: Unquantified. Conflicting canonical signals can make a search engine's canonical selection for /services less predictable, and the rendered target points to a different page (/booking). No indexing, ranking, lead or booking impact is claimed: provider index state and Google-selected canonical are unknown.
findings.description: Observed in one supplied synthetic capture of https://atlas.example/services (profile mobile, state anonymous, captured 2026-11-19T11:30:00Z, valid until 2026-11-19T12:30:00Z): the source-head layer declares canonical https://atlas.example/services while the rendered-head layer declares https://atlas.example/booking; the HTTP Link layer is complete with no canonical target. All three layers are marked complete, so the evaluator recorded canonical-consistency as fail (conflicting-declared-targets). The capture does not identify which script, template or rewrite produces the difference, and it is not authenticated production behaviour.
findings.recommendation: First obtain the owner's preferred canonical for /services (request owner-intent). Then have website engineering identify the mechanism that changes the canonical between source and rendered head and make all declared layers agree on the owner-approved target. Do not change the site as part of this audit.
findings.title: Conflicting canonical declarations between source head and rendered head on /services
findings.verification: Supply a fresh canonical-capture-v1 for https://atlas.example/services (mobile, anonymous) with complete source-head, rendered-head and HTTP Link layers inside a new declared window; re-run enterprise-technical-seo-evaluate and confirm canonical-consistency passes and, once a concrete owner expectation exists, canonical-owner-intent passes. Confirm provider-selected canonical separately with a scoped URL Inspection export.

methodology: Coverage concerns declared checks, not every possible website defect.
Historical measurements are retained separately from current observations.
Structural validation and attributed review do not independently authenticate provider data.
No raw evidence payloads are included; inspect the source run using its recorded digest.
Redaction requires review; pattern matching is not a guarantee that every confidential value was identified.

narrative.text: Scope: one synthetic page target (https://atlas.example/services, mobile, anonymous) for customer atlas-demo, entity website, evidence window 2026-11-19T11:00:00Z (inclusive) to 12:00:00Z (exclusive), assessment time 2026-11-19T12:00:00Z, inventory mode sample. No content inventory, page text, GA4, Search Console, Bing, GTM, consent policy, performance or accessibility evidence was supplied, so the content-quality, SEO-content, AIO, AEO and GEO dimensions and the measurement modules were not assessed and remain unknown. Absent analytics is not zero performance.
Observed: the source-head layer (complete) lists the canonical target "https://atlas.example/services" (page-capture.json:16).
Observed: the rendered-head layer (complete) lists a different canonical target "https://atlas.example/booking" (page-capture.json:22).
Observed: the HTTP Link layer is complete with "targets": [] (page-capture.json:27), i.e. no Link-header canonical was declared in this capture.

Evaluator results for this capture: canonical-target-format pass (both observed targets are valid absolute URLs without fragments); canonical-consistency fail (two distinct declared targets); canonical-owner-intent unknown (no owner expectation supplied); provider-index-state unknown (a local capture cannot establish indexing or Google-selected canonical). The capture was fresh at assessment (captured 11:30:00Z, max age 3600 s, valid until 12:30:00Z). Its SHA-256 establishes integrity of the supplied bytes, not authenticity.

Failed collection attempt recorded: attempt-one, collector synthetic-export-1, started 2026-11-19T11:35:00Z, finished 2026-11-19T11:36:00Z, status unknown, gap "browser-unavailable" (collection-attempt.json:18), synthetic, executionAuthenticated false, semanticAcceptance false. It produced no capture, so capture availability for target services-canonical-browser is unknown (capture-unavailable). No page observations were inferred from the attempt metadata; the separately supplied page capture is the only canonical evidence and was not produced by this attempt.

The brief states: The owner has supplied no preferred canonical policy. (brief.md:6). Owner intent therefore remains unknown and is requested from the SEO owner; this audit does not infer the intended canonical from the observed page.

Priority: (1) SEO owner supplies the preferred canonical for /services; (2) website engineering investigates the source-versus-rendered canonical discrepancy and aligns all layers to the approved target; (3) retry the authorized browser capture under a new window; (4) Search Console owner supplies a URL Inspection export. All actions are proposals; no site change, form submission or external contact was performed.

Limitations: single synthetic capture; supplied projections not verified against native HTML, DOM or headers; no reachability, content-equivalence, indexing or ranking claim; no aggregation across devices, states or other URLs; report brand accent is a neutral placeholder because no customer brand profile was supplied; no independent review decision has been recorded, so no claim is accepted.
